ownership.notes: Privately held; the ultimate parent is Bytedance Ltd. (Cayman Islands) per its FY2025 Spain country-by-country report, which states the parent "has not made available information with respect to the Group's worldwide operations". Board: Liang Rubo (chairman), Arthur Dantchik, William E. Ford, Xavier Niel, Neil Shen; named investors include Sequoia Capital, General Atlantic, SoftBank Vision Fund, KKR and Tiger Global. The US TikTok business sits in TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC (from 2026-01-22), in which ByteDance holds 19.9%. Volcano Engine (火山引擎) is its cloud unit, contracting as 北京火山引擎科技有限公司.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: ByteDance is China's largest data-centre tenant and — on Chinese suppliers' own filings, not its own word — a direct buyer of data-centre power equipment, but it names no power vendor, publishes no accounts, and its one reported move toward 800 VDC is a tender, not an award. SemiAnalysis's China model (25 Sep 2026) puts it at roughly a fifth of China's delivered data-centre capacity, nearly all rented; the acquirer of Chindata China discloses that one unnamed customer took 90.12% of that landlord's 2025 revenue, and the same filing identifies that customer's own campuses as Volcano Engine projects. Its 2026 capex is known only from anonymous-source leaks that differ in scope as well as size — a preliminary RMB 160B (Financial Times, Dec 2025), more than RMB 200B (SCMP, May 2026) and up to US$70B under discussion (Bloomberg, May 2026) — and ByteDance has confirmed none of them. BACKGROUND: Founded in 2012 by a team led by Zhang Yiming and Liang Rubo; ultimate parent Bytedance Ltd. (Cayman Islands); operational headquarters Beijing. The consumer platforms (Douyin, TikTok, CapCut, Toutiao) are the demand base; Volcano Engine (火山引擎) sells cloud, GPU compute and the Doubao/Seed models in China, and BytePlus abroad. Per leaks, not filings: 2025 revenue about US$200B and H1 2026 revenue about US$120B with net profit about US$20B (The Information, as relayed in September 2026); an earlier aggregator figure for 2025 is US$186B. The US TikTok business moved into TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC on 22 Jan 2026 — Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX 15% each, ByteDance 19.9%. Named power-equipment suppliers in exchange filings are Kstar (UPS and power modules), TGOOD (prefabricated substations), Mingyang Electric (power modules), Jinpan (transformers), Sifang (protection and energy management) and Zhonhen (precision distribution); no Megmeet, Sinexcel or Kehua filing names ByteDance. Collection gap: ByteDance's own channels say nothing about data-centre power architecture; every procurement fact here comes from a counterparty.
ecosystemRole: We assess ByteDance as the demand anchor of China's wholesale data-centre market and a three-door buyer of power equipment. Door one is its own campuses, run under the Volcano Engine name — Wuhu/Wuwei in Anhui, Taihang in Datong, Horinger in Inner Mongolia, with Ulanqab (5–6 GW, in talks) and Zhongwei next — where suppliers' filings record ByteDance buying UPS and power modules, prefabricated substations, transformers and precision distribution directly. Door two is its landlords' build-to-suit halls: Chindata China (about 90% of revenue from one customer whose self-build list is Volcano Engine's), VNET (510 MW from 'a leading internet customer' Bloomberg names as ByteDance) and Range. Door three runs through the landlord's tender: Chindata's acquirer states that for equipment it tenders among the vendors on the customer's qualified-vendor list and then buys that vendor's UPS, so a UPS vendor must be on the tenant's approved list even when the landlord signs the order. Overseas it leases (Bridge Data Centres in Johor, Green Mountain in Norway, Omnia in Brazil) and rents GPU capacity (Oracle's ASEAN fleet per SemiAnalysis; Aolani in Malaysia per the WSJ). For a power-electronics seller the relevant fact is not the capex headline but which door a given hall sits behind, because the person who writes the specification differs by door. Basis: supplier and landlord exchange filings, SemiAnalysis, trade press; ByteDance itself discloses none of it.

productsAndServices.name: Volcano Engine MaaS — Volcano Ark (火山方舟) and the Doubao-Seed models

Doubao usage reached 180 trillion tokens a day by June 2026, per Volcano Engine president Tan Dai at the Force conference. Per 36Kr (June 2026), the 2026 MaaS revenue target was raised to RMB 15B and Seedance 2.0 exceeded RMB 1B in a month.

IDC: Volcano Engine held 49.2% of China's public-cloud LLM token calls in H1 2025 (Alibaba Cloud 27%, Baidu 17%)
On revenue the ranking reverses: Omdia and Frost & Sullivan put Alibaba Cloud first in China enterprise MaaS in H1 2025 (35.8% and 30.2%), per DoNews

productsAndServices.positioning: Volcano Engine leads on token volume and competes on price against Alibaba Cloud, Baidu AI Cloud and Tencent Cloud; Alibaba leads on MaaS revenue. The two metrics tell opposite stories and the dossier reports both.

productsAndServices.roadmap: Doubao 2.1 series launched at Force 2026 (23 Jun 2026); Seed releases through Aug 2026 (Seedance 2.5, Seed Audio 1.0, a full-duplex audio-visual LLM)

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that ByteDance buys data-centre power equipment through three doors, and that a seller who does not know which door a hall sits behind is selling to the wrong person. Basis: suppliers' filings record direct ByteDance purchases for its own Volcano Engine campuses (Kstar UPS and power modules, TGOOD prefabricated substations, Mingyang power modules, Sifang protection, Far East cable); Zhonhen records precision-distribution wins in 'third-party co-built rooms' — ByteDance buying inside a landlord's building; and Chindata's acquirer states that UPS vendors are chosen from the customer's qualified-vendor list even when the landlord places the order. The door decides who writes the specification.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that ByteDance's 800 VDC move is a tender signal, not yet a programme. Basis: the only numbers in circulation — HVDC at 30–40% penetration and a building-level, tens-of-MW 800 V pilot — trace to one unattributed expo post of 22 Jan 2026; the same site said a week later that the 800 V work was 'still out to tender'; 21世纪经济报道 confirmed on 22 Sep only that 800 V HVDC was 'first introduced'; no filing by any listed supplier announces a ByteDance 800 V or SST award. Indicator to watch: the first supplier filing or company release naming a ByteDance 800 V or SST award — its absence through the Q3 2026 reports (due by 31 Oct) would confirm the pilot has not been let.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the capex figures bracket a budget and a ceiling rather than disagree. Basis: the FT's RMB 160B (Dec 2025) and SCMP's 'more than RMB 200B' (May 2026) are framed as the planned budget, the second a revision of the first; Bloomberg's 'up to US$70B' (May 2026) is total capex under discussion, 'preliminary and subject to adjustment'. The spread is about 3× low to high. Two dated facts set the scale independently: a US$29.6B loan (Sep 2026) and H1 2026 profit of about US$20B (The Information). ByteDance has confirmed none of these.

(High confidence) We assess that self-build is the direction of travel and the landlords' main risk. Basis: Chindata's acquirer discloses that Customer A takes about 90% of revenue, that the first wholesale contract expires in November 2027 with no renewal talks started, and it tabulates Customer A's own Volcano Engine campuses (Wuhu 306 MW and 335 MW, Taihang phase 2 ~187 MW, Horinger 220 MW) as a risk; SemiAnalysis counts three self-build clusters and a fourth forming; SCMP reports 5–6 GW of talks in Ulanqab. Self-build moves the power-equipment decision from the landlord's engineers to ByteDance's.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that ByteDance's named power suppliers are domestic distribution, UPS and substation makers, not the NVIDIA-roster rack-power vendors. Basis: every filing that names ByteDance as a customer comes from Kstar, TGOOD, Mingyang Electric, Jinpan, Sifang, Far East or Zhonhen; a full-text search of Megmeet, Sinexcel and Kehua filings finds no ByteDance mention, and Kehua anonymises its internet customers. Collection gap: absence from filings is not absence of business — Chinese suppliers routinely anonymise hyperscale customers.

(Low confidence) We assess that ByteDance's most advanced racks may be designed around its own accelerators rather than imported GPUs, which would make ByteDance — not a GPU vendor's reference design — the author of its rack power envelope. Basis: reported, not confirmed — Qualcomm manufacturing ByteDance-designed ASICs (Bloomberg via RCR Tech, May 2026), a larger domestic-chip budget (SCMP, May 2026), and Beijing rationing imported H200s (about 10,000 delivered by August 2026). Indicator to watch: any ByteDance or Volcano Engine statement of a rack power class or busbar voltage.

relationships.scale: 90.12% of Chindata China 2025 revenue (Customer A, identity inferred)
relationships.note: Chindata China's 'Customer A' — about 90% of its revenue — is identified in the acquirer's own filing only by a list of Volcano Engine self-build campuses; ByteDance was 86.3% of Chindata's revenue in 2022 when it still filed in the US.
relationships.context: HEC's reply to the SSE inquiry (23 Sep 2026) gives Customer A at 91.00% of 2024, 90.12% of 2025 and 90.22% of Jan–Feb 2026 revenue, on contracts 'mostly 10 years and longer', and in the section on Customer A's own build plans lists 火山引擎长三角算力中心, 长三角无为算力中心, 火山云太行算力中心 and 内蒙古和林格尔算力中心 — all Volcano Engine projects. The filing never names Customer A, and Chindata's own profile page gives lower shares (80.23% for 2024, 83.54% for Jan–May 2025), which may reflect different aggregation of entities under common control; no source reconciles the two. The first wholesale contract expires in November 2027. ByteDance is also the anchor tenant of MY06 in Johor, operated by the now-separate Bridge Data Centres.

relationships.note: Zhonhen's 2025 annual report records precision-distribution wins at 'ByteDance self-built rooms and several third-party co-built rooms'.
relationships.context: The win is precision distribution, not HVDC — the HVDC win named in the same passage is Bank of China — and Zhonhen's H1 2026 interim does not mention ByteDance. Jinpan's inquiry reply of October 2025 separately lists ByteDance among Zhonhen's end-customers. Retail-blog claims that Zhonhen is ByteDance's 'core supplier' or covers its Ulanqab campus appear in no filing.

relationships.note: Narada's July 2026 AIDC release names ByteDance among the long-term partners of its backup-power business.
relationships.context: The statement is a company press release, not an exchange filing — Narada's 2025 annual report and H1 2026 interim do not mention ByteDance. It names no product, date or volume.

relationships.note: ByteDance buys Nvidia accelerators within US licences and Beijing approvals; about 10,000 H200s were delivered by August 2026.
relationships.context: The FT (Dec 2025) reported RMB 85B of the preliminary 2026 plan for AI processors and a preliminary 20,000-unit H200 order; the US approved H200 sales to about ten Chinese firms including ByteDance in May 2026, up to 75,000 units each, and Beijing conditions each purchase. Frontier Nvidia hardware is also rented abroad (Aolani in Malaysia; Oracle's ASEAN capacity per SemiAnalysis).

relationships.note: Oracle is a 15% managing investor and 'Trusted Security Partner' of TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, in which ByteDance holds 19.9%; the JV runs in Oracle's US cloud.
relationships.context: TikTok's announcement (23 Jan 2026) names Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX as managing investors at 15% each and gives ByteDance 19.9%; Oracle EVP Kenneth Glueck sits on the seven-member board. Separately, SemiAnalysis (June 2025) wrote that 'most of Oracle's ASEAN GPU capacity' is believed allocated to ByteDance — a single-outlet estimate.

relationships.note: MGX holds 15% of TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC as a managing investor; ByteDance holds 19.9%.
relationships.context: MGX's David Scott sits on the JV board and its security committee. The corpus's MGX dossier records the same stakes.

relationships.note: Volcano Engine competes with Alibaba Cloud in China's cloud and model-API market — first on token volume, second on revenue.
relationships.context: IDC gave Volcano Engine 49.2% of China's public-cloud LLM token calls in H1 2025 against Alibaba Cloud's 27%; on revenue, Omdia and Frost & Sullivan put Alibaba Cloud first in enterprise MaaS. Both are also China's two largest reported AI-infrastructure spenders in 2026 and compete for the same wholesale landlords.

policyExposure.exposure: The Supreme Court upheld the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act in TikTok Inc. v. Garland (17 Jan 2025). The US business now sits in TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, with ByteDance capped at 19.9%, a majority-American board and Oracle as security partner; ByteDance keeps global interoperability and e-commerce, advertising and marketing activities.

US approvals for H200 sales to about ten Chinese firms including ByteDance, up to 75,000 units each (May 2026); Beijing conditions each purchase, and about 10,000 H200s had been delivered by August 2026. The FT reported that ByteDance leases overseas data centres to reach Nvidia hardware legally, booked as opex.
policyExposure.mitigation: Overseas leasing and GPU rental (Johor, Oracle ASEAN); a larger domestic-chip budget (SCMP, May 2026).

policyExposure.regime: East Data, West Computing (东数西算)
policyExposure.exposure: SemiAnalysis calls the Wuhu cluster an East-Data-West-Computing cluster serving east-China inference and places the two Zhongwei (Ningxia) entities registered in July 2026 in another EDWC region — the self-build map follows the national hub nodes.
